identity.operation: Parse an element with PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE selected.
identity.condition: An element contains whitespace-only text before its closing tag.
identity.capability: The XMLDocument whitespace mode can select PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE and retain the whitespace text node.
identity.consequence: The requested whitespace text node cannot be retained through this mode.

requirement: Parse an element such as <r>  </r> with PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE, retaining the whitespace text node.

assessment.necessity_reason: For <r>  </r>, PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE creates a text node from the spaces before </r>. The harness always constructs the document with the default PRESERVE_WHITESPACE mode. Input bytes cannot change that constructor choice, and the default path skips those spaces.

before.requirement: Parse an element with PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE selected and retain its whitespace-only text immediately before the closing tag.
before.reason: The pedantic path is supported, but the harness constructs only a default-mode document.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Declares PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE as a selectable mode.
The document constructor defaults to PRESERVE_WHITESPACE.
The selected change group concerns cleanup of parsed child nodes.

after.requirement: Parse an element with PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE selected and retain its whitespace-only text immediately before the closing tag.
after.reason: The pedantic path remains supported; the same harness still fixes the document to the default mode.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Declares PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE as a selectable mode.
The document constructor defaults to PRESERVE_WHITESPACE.
The changed destructor cleans up parsed child nodes.

assessment.comparison_reason: The same default-only document construction prevents selection of PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE on both sides. The parser condition for retaining the whitespace text is unchanged.

necessity_evidence.reason: The same coverage gap exists before and after the change. The parser supports a distinct PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE result, but the fixed harness always constructs a default PRESERVE_WHITESPACE document. The changed destructor concerns cleanup and does not change that blocker.
necessity_evidence.finite_witness: The valid input <r>  </r> retains the two spaces as a text child when parsed with XMLDocument(true, PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE). The old harness can supply those bytes but cannot select that document mode.

scope_contract.reason: The target's primary operation is XMLDocument::Parse, whose document configuration includes a supported whitespace mode. This behavior belongs to the parser's operational surface even though the harness currently uses the default.

feasible_trigger.reason: With PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE selected, the finite XML input <r>  </r> meets the first-child, intervening-whitespace, and closing-tag conditions. The harness accepts those bytes, but its constructor fixes the mode to the default.

evidence.dependency_reason: The element parser passes first=true to Identify for its first child.
The constructor supports PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE but defaults to PRESERVE_WHITESPACE.

observable_consequence.reason: Pedantic mode creates an XMLText node from the literal spaces and inserts it as the element's child. Default mode skips those spaces before recognizing the closing element, so the target cannot reach that supported DOM result through this mode.

evidence.dependency_reason: Identify skips whitespace before choosing a node type.
A successfully parsed text node is inserted into the DOM.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete entry has one default document construction and one Parse call; input bytes cannot change the constructor argument. Entity references or CDATA can produce whitespace text, but neither selects PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE nor exercises its literal-whitespace condition.

evidence.dependency_reason: Omitting the whitespace argument selects PRESERVE_WHITESPACE.
Entity processing can alter text content but does not select the pedantic parsing branch.

identity_preserved.reason: The same tuple—pedantic parsing of literal whitespace immediately before a closing tag—is supported on both source versions and blocked by the same default-only harness. The g0001 destructor change affects cleanup of nodes, not whitespace-mode selection.

evidence.dependency_reason: The before destructor deletes child nodes.
The changed destructor still deletes child nodes.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: PEDANTIC_WHITESPACE retains literal whitespace-only text immediately before an element's closing tag as an XMLText child.
coverage_witness.actual_target_setup: Construct XMLDocument with no arguments, selecting PRESERVE_WHITESPACE, then call Parse on the fuzzer-supplied string.
coverage_witness.blocked_behavior: The target cannot select pedantic mode and retain the two literal spaces through its pedantic parsing branch.
coverage_witness.equivalent_routes: None in this entry. Encoded whitespace and CDATA do not select pedantic mode or exercise its literal-whitespace condition.
